data.content_ref: inline:The argument asserts the §11.3 flag should be lifted because repeated critic failure on a single artifact (SRC_005) is more economically explained by test-design deficiency than by critic deficiency. But this defense is self-defeating under the audit standard: it concedes that both critics in fact failed on the very artifact they were tasked with adjudicating, and it provides no premise warranting that a critic's failure is excused merely because a co-evaluated critic also fails. The proposed mechanist stance is a bare interpretive lens ('the most economical causal explanation is...'), not an audit rule; §11.3 does not condition flag-sustention on uniqueness of failure mode across critics, so even granting the shared-structural-assumption hypothesis leaves the sustained flag intact for each critic individually.
